back: Order = highest order of derivative present.
Degree = power of the highest-order derivative, provided the equation is polynomial in derivatives.
An n-th-order DE has a general solution with n arbitrary constants.
A specific solution satisfying given initial/boundary conditions; constants are then fixed.
dy/dx = f(x)g(y) ⇒ (1/g) dy = f dx; integrate both sides independently.

dy/dx + P(x) y = Q(x). Solution via integrating factor μ = e^{∫P dx}; then (μ y)' = μ Q, integrate.
μ(x) = e^{∫ P(x) dx}; multiply through by μ to get (μ y)' = μ Q.

front: Solution of y'' + a y' + b y = 0
back: Form the characteristic equation r² + a r + b = 0. Real distinct roots ⇒ exponential sum; repeated ⇒ t e^(rt); complex α ± iβ ⇒ e^(αt)(C₁ cos βt + C₂ sin βt).
Find the complementary function from the homogeneous part, then a particular integral (PI) by a suitable trial using undetermined coefficients.
Differentiate the family equation n times (once per arbitrary constant) and eliminate constants to obtain the DE of order n.

back: If the equation gives dx/dy more easily, solve for x(y) by treating it as a first-order linear/separable equation in y.
